title: Psychology of Human Relationships Adventure 2: Breakdown — Duck's Phases
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace Duck's four phases of relationship breakdown.
meta_desc: IBDP Psychology Human Relationships: Duck's (1982/2007) model of relationship breakdown.
final_note: You sequenced Duck's four phases and explained each transition.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Steve Duck (1982) modelled breakdown in four phases.

1. Intrapsychic — one partner privately broods on dissatisfaction.
2. Dyadic — concerns voiced to partner; conflict or repair attempted.

3. Social — break-up made public; friends choose sides; reputational concerns matter.
4. Grave-dressing — each partner constructs a story of why the relationship ended, often blaming the other to protect self-image.

Duck & Rollie (2007) added a fifth phase: resurrection — building a new identity and approach for future relationships.

Critique: model is descriptive, not predictive; ignores positive break-ups; based largely on heterosexual Western couples.
